bull.b: Rapid revenue growth and a large contracted backlog provide substantial visibility into future demand. Continued customer commitments and expanding power capacity support durable scale in AI infrastructure over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Strong Unit Economics and Operating Leverage
bull.b: Healthy gross margins, positive EBITDA, and rising operating cash generation indicate attractive core economics as infrastructure utilization increases. Scaling can improve cost absorption and support stronger operating profitability over time.

Growth in managed inference broadens CoreWeave beyond raw GPU capacity toward higher-value platform services. This can deepen customer integration, diversify revenue, and strengthen recurring demand as enterprise AI adoption expands.

bear.b: The heavily debt-funded capital structure limits financial flexibility and increases refinancing and interest-rate exposure. Any slowdown in customer utilization or renewals could make debt servicing and further capacity funding more difficult.

bear.t: Heavy Capital Intensity and Negative Free Cash Flow
bear.b: CoreWeave’s expansion requires exceptionally large upfront investment in GPUs and facilities, while operating cash flow does not yet cover spending. Sustained negative free cash flow increases dependence on financing and execution discipline.

Despite strong gross profit and EBITDA, depreciation, operating costs, and financing expense prevent bottom-line profitability. Rising interest costs could delay earnings conversion and reduce the cash available to reinvest or deleverage.
